themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing you are measuring often changes while you measure it. So the usual first move is to build a small truth set of your own, or admit you are only estimating.
themes.evidence: On identity resolution all three models say there is no independent answer key for whether two records are the same person, and consent rules block assembling the data that would prove it; the same gap drives answer engine optimization (no impressions, no stable rank), cross-channel incrementality (platforms change the treatment mid-test), and B2B buying-group signal loss (outcomes arrive quarters late and only for accounts already chosen).

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the person or company holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and no one can make them. A shared schema or standard cannot settle a fight over money, credit, or turf.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models agree agents have a selfish reason to pose as humans and no one can force honest disclosure; on the semantic context layer they call conflicting definitions of customer a political settlement, not a modeling gap; on journey orchestration the blocker is channel owners paid on their own conversions; on incrementality platforms have no reason to expose how treatment was assigned.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, or a message leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. Compliance and effects can only be estimated from outside, never proven.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion all three models say enforcement ends at the boundary: ad platforms and partners expose no lineage, membership, or deletion evidence, and a person's contribution to a trained model can be diluted but not located; identity work hits the same wall when false matches must be judged across closed platforms.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Every model answering safe agent execution proposes the same thing, a proxy or gateway in front of all writes with its own credentials, logging, caps, and a kill switch; the downstream consent answers reach for one gate on every data egress path, and journey orchestration proposes a single shared pre-send eligibility check.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set fully captures that. The models end up shrinking human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance all three build a locked library of approved claims because deciding whether wording crosses a legal line is a reasoning task software cannot defend in an audit; the semantic context layer answers make the parallel point that context-dependent meaning cannot be flattened into one global definition.
